The old fashioned way to install and remove .deb packages is

sudo dpkg -i package_name.deb # installs
sudo dpkg -r package_name # removes

Alternatively, double clicking a deb should install it and the installed package should be somewhere in the software manager. The only stuff that's safe to manually delete is the stuff you can delete using a file manager without super user permissions.

In the future:

  • Place /home on it's own partition, giving it the lions share of disk space - this is where personalization, media, games, programs, etc reside.

  • Add your user to the Plex group, add plex to your user group. This allows your user and plex to operate as eachother, bypassing many possible hiccups.

  • sudo apt-get autoremove [application] will remove dependencies that were installed specifically for the app (dependencies that only have ties to that application)

  • sudo apt-get purge [application] - removes the app and anything it created on your system (configs, etc) that reside outside your home folder (/home/RedSocks157/)

If you keep /home on it's own partition, I have found that this makes a "fresh install" so much quicker nad less painful.

As for your specific issue, sadly, I would suggest backing up whatever you can and nuking it. This is a learning experience, and it's only difficult because you don't remember how long it took you to learn windows. Chill, go have a drink, come back when you aren't as frustrated.
